insights.headline: Gold heads for a second weekly loss as payrolls loom and yields hit 2002 highs
insights.summary: Gold slipped toward $4,155 an ounce on Friday, on track for a second straight weekly decline of more than 3% as the US payrolls report due at 1230 GMT keeps rate-hike bets alive. The dollar held a 17-month high and US 10-year yields touched their highest since 2002, while in India the 10-year benchmark closed at a 2.5-year high of 7.21% with an RBI hike expected next week. MCX stays fully closed on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti, and silver is testing a $60.84 pivot as festive demand builds toward Diwali.
points: Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,154.78 ahead of US payrolls; a hot print could revive Fed hike bets, says Capital.com's Kyle Rodda.
Dollar index at a 17-month high of 102.08; US 10-year yield hit 5.344% Thursday, its highest since 2002; euro at weakest since May 2025.
India's 10-year yield closed at 7.21%, a 2.5-year high, with an RBI hike expected next week; the bond market is shut Friday for Gandhi Jayanti.
MCX is fully closed on October 2 (both sessions); trading resumes Monday, October 5. Indian banks booked $500M in FX losses after RBI position curbs.
Silver (XAG) is testing the $60.84 pivot even as Sierra Madre scales up mine supply; festive buying toward Diwali may cushion dips.

items.title: 10-year bond yield breaches 7.20%; hits 2.5-year high
items.summary: India's 10-year benchmark bond yield breached 7.20% to close at 7.21%, its highest in two and a half years, as elevated crude prices and expectations of an RBI rate hike next week weighed. ET reports the RBI is expected to raise rates by 25 bps to 5.50%, though Ujjivan Small Finance Bank's Rajeev Pawar said markets appear to be pricing a 50 bps move. items.title: Stock market holiday on Oct 2: MCX fully closed for Gandhi Jayanti
items.summary: NSE and BSE stay closed on Friday, October 2 for Gandhi Jayanti, with no trading across equity, derivatives or SLB segments. MCX will also remain fully closed — both the morning (9am-5pm) and evening sessions — and banks across the country are shut. Normal trading resumes Monday, October 5 after the long weekend; MCX sees a partial holiday on Dussehra (Oct 20) and Muhurat trading on Diwali...

items.title: US dollar climbs to 17-month high as global bond rout hits euro
items.summary: The dollar index held at a 17-month high of 102.08, headed for a third straight weekly gain, as the bond rout pushed the US 10-year yield to 5.344% Thursday — its highest since 2002. The euro fell to $1.1237, its lowest since May 2025, on French fiscal worries, while Brent traded above $100. Saxo's Charu Chanana said the move reflects term premium and fiscal risk, not just Fed expectations.

items.title: Indian banks faced $500 million FX losses after RBI position curbs
items.summary: Indian banks booked roughly $500 million in foreign-exchange trading losses after the RBI's curbs on net open currency positions forced them to unwind large rupee bets. The caps, aimed at steadying the rupee near record lows as crude topped $100, mark a shift from direct market intervention to regulatory tightening.

items.title: New gold ETF folios collapse from 12 lakh in January to ~4,000 as first-time buyers drift to digital gold
items.summary: Investors opened 12 lakh new gold ETF folios in January at the cycle peak; by late summer net new folios ran at roughly 4,000 a month. August inflows still rose 67% to ₹2,597 crore, but from existing investors — institutions hold most ETF assets. Digital gold via UPI apps averaged ₹2,500 crore a month from June to August, up 110% year on year.

items.title: Silver (XAG) Forecast: 10-Year Yield Reversal Puts $60.84 Pivot Back in Play
items.summary: Silver reclaimed the $60.84 pivot as the 10-year Treasury yield reversed from its highs and October Fed-hike odds fell to about 33% after the soft PCE report, FXEmpire's technical read says. With the dollar still firm near its peak, Friday's non-farm payrolls are the next test; a break above $61.73 would turn the minor trend up.

items.title: Silver Falls 45% From Its 2026 Peak as Sierra Madre Scales Up Production
items.summary: Silver has fallen about 45% from its January peak near $115 an ounce to around $63 by mid-September, a company-backed analysis notes, even as the World Silver Survey 2026 reports a fifth straight annual supply deficit of 40.3 million ounces in 2025. Metals Focus expects another 46.3-million-ounce shortfall in 2026.

items.title: Gold, silver prices edge higher: How festive demand could shape the outlook
items.summary: Domestic gold and silver futures edged higher ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, CNBC-TV18 reports, quoting analysts on how festive demand could shape the near-term price outlook.

items.title: Gold price future roadmap: What led to 6% yellow metal fall in Sept 2026? Will Diwali help bounce back? Experts view
items.summary: Mint's market experts trace September's roughly 6% fall in gold to surging US bond yields, a strong dollar and rate-hike repricing, and ask whether Diwali-season buying can engineer a rebound. The piece weighs festive demand against still-elevated prices as Indian buyers head into the peak buying season.
